Firstly who was the deputy chief of the basic crime section at Zadar-Knin Police Administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Formally, it did not have a deputy; although a person was assigned to -- to the post, and I can't remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And what was to happen with this information that was being sent?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: This is precisely the information that we collected from police stations and which we were duty-bound to forward to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look now at the next page in this document, page 3 -- or page 2 in the -- page 2 in the Croatian --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see from the 6th Police Station in Benkovac, dated the 2nd of September, from Mr. Saponja, and it refers to co-operation between the police station in Benkovac and the military police as being good as efficient. And complaints and poor co-operation have not been present. And then it refers to reports concerning the setting of family houses on fire of people who are of Serbian origin, as well as reports about demolition and taking away other people's property, although in less proportion, and the ... police is undertaking necessary measures. And returning the figures of five arson, two serious larceny, as on-site investigations completed, and that -- this was being delivered to Zadar-Knin. So what would happen with this information, Mr. Cetina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: The information was processed and sent to the Ministry of the Interior, as part of one compound report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just taking that police station in Benkovac, are you able to say, for instance, how many police officers worked at a police station such as that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, between 70 -- anything between 70, 80, or 90.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the area that it covered? Are you able to help us with that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: I don't know what the size of the area was, but it was an area that bordered with the Zadar territory. It is closer to Zadar than to Knin and other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May that document be made an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit D1750. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1750 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to Exhibit D576, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document from you. It's a report, as requested from the original order of Mr. Moric. It's dated the 2nd of September and concerns burning houses, removal of property. And it refers to the co-operation of the police with the military police "is inadequate in the entire area." And that this issue was analysed at a meeting of the Knin district police station commanders and the MUP coordinator on the 30th of August in Gracac. Can you tell us, was that a meeting with the military police, or was it a meeting just of the civil police?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: I can't remember at this point. However, it -- it is probable that the police ourselves, we, ourselves, held the meeting on our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it took place in Gracac with the MUP coordinator. Who was that, on the 30th of August?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: I would have to rely on what the text says because I don't remember. It is in the plural, all the coordinators who were present in the police stations located in the liberated territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it was all the police station commanders, as well as coordinators were at this meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As the text shows, there was criticism of the military police and the shortages of units of the 71st and of the 72nd. How was this criticism of the military police dealt with? What -- here you are at a meeting of the civilian police. You identify this problem in their performance. What was done about it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: We could inform the ministry thereof, and we didn't have any other option.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time, your police administration had also been ordered to have meetings with the military police commanders. Were your problems and criticisms expressed directly to the military police by your police administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Always at the meetings, we raised the problems that we had informed the ministry of in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn now to Exhibit P2206.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a report, analysis, submitted by the military police administration, on the 12th of September, 1995, and sent to the military police battalions, including the 71st and 72nd. And it's an analysis by them of the co-operation between the MUP and the military police between the 22nd of August and 31st of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 4 in the English and page 4 in the Croatian where we see the comment on the Zadar-Knin Police Administration that has been put in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it's written here "Zadar-Knin Police Administration." And it says: "The co-operation is not satisfactory, and quite inadequate in the area of Knin, Obrovac, and Gracac, where they have not been included at the check-points." Looking at that comment, what would you say about that assertion that you weren't in -- your police administration wasn't including the military police at the check-points?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: This is the first time I am seeing this. Well, of course, the ministry forwarded all the information they received from us to the military police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, was it right that your police weren't including the military police at check-points?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Well, we would have been glad and content had they manned all the check-points that were necessary. This isn't correct that we didn't include them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After the Zadar-Knin Police Administration, it deals with the Knin Police Administration, although we've seen the area of Knin has already been referred to. And it says, on page 5 of the English: "Knin police administration. The problem of co-operation is the same as Zadar-Knin Police Administration." Would you care to comment on that, whether the Knin police administration was also not including the military police on check-points? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: They would surely have included them, had they provided the necessary men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go to D581, Exhibit D581.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Another report by you to Mr. Moric on the subject of co-operation, dated the 12th of September, 1995. It says here the co-operation between the various police administrations, stations, is decent but inadequate. Problems occur in the implementation of agreements because there is no co-operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've got the wrong document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This isn't the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit D581. There we are. That's the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is your report to Mr. Moric on co-operation. And it -- it refers to eliminating problems at daily meetings between the police stations. "Personnel of the military police are short of personnel ... some check-points do not have a presence." Again, was that because you were not including them at check-points, or because they didn't have enough personnel?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: No. We would certainly have included them, had they provided the necessary personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there a meeting that you attended in a hotel at the Plitvice Lakes on the 15th of September, which was a joint meeting of the MUP and the military police?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you express there your view about the problems with co-operation with the military police in your area?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can look at Exhibit D595 and turn to page 4 of the English, page 3 of the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see Colonel Budimir refers to the large area covered by the 72nd Military Police and didn't agree with opinions that there was not enough manpower. I won't ask about that. But the area covered by the 72nd Military Police, are you able to help us with that? What was the extent of their territorial responsibility?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: The structure and the area of responsibility of the military police was not organised in the same way as that of the police. Therefore, the areas covered by the 71st and the 72nd Battalions coincide with the territories of the entire Splitsko-Dalmatinska, Zadarsko-Kninska, Licko-Sinjska, and Primorsko-Gorinska Police Administrations. I do believe, indeed, that they did not have enough personnel to cover the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can now look at another document which is on the same subject but a different topic, Exhibit D802.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And this is a record from the military police administration concerning Operative Action Varivode between the 6th of October and 10th of October, 1995. This report is dated the 11th of October. And we can see that there was a meeting of people involved in Operative Action Varivode at the Zadar-Knin Police Administration, which included yourself and Mr. Bitanga and other members of the MUP, as well as, on behalf of the military police administration, Colonel Kozic, Major Ivan Juric, Captain Eluga [phoen]. And I now want to ask you about this particular matter. What was Operative Action Varivode? How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: It was an action carried out in connection with the criminal investigation for the suspected murders in the places of Varivode and Gosici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was this a joint initiative between the MUP and the military police?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: I suppose so, because senior officers of the military police and the civilian police force were engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had any similar initiative to this happened before?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the document, we can see, on page 2 in the English, Chief Djurica in the Zadar-Knin Police Administration. And if we can have page 2 of the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Discuss the current general security situation in the field and measures undertaken, and specific points are -- are made of how the military police and MUP are to work, staff of ordinary and special police with check-points. And it's set out, further on, about patrol cars. And it has a goal. And if we turn to page 3 in the English, we can see the level of discussion and specific details that are referred to. And as a result of the check-points, we see a number of figures, of people who are checked, vehicles searched. Page 4 of the English. Details of arrests that were -- were made, people warned, what was confiscated. And we can see the detail of how things operated. What sort of area did Operation Varivode cover? Was it throughout the Zadar-Knin Police Administration, or was it in a more local position? What did it cover?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: In fact, one could say that it was the first step leading to a higher quality co-operation between the military police and the civilian police, and it led to the resolution of these criminal cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could these measures have been applied throughout the whole of the area of your police administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. With this sort of organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to comment at all as to why it didn't happen before between the MUP and the military police, that you operated in -- in this way, as you did with Varivode?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: In my view, the sole reason was the absence of co-operation -- the fact that no co-operation was forthcoming from the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I have just finished this matter as well, Your Honour. That is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I would -- first I would like to ask Madam Usher to escort Mr. Cetina out of the courtroom. We will have a break, Mr. Cetina. We'd like to see you back in 20 to 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I would like to deliver the Chamber's reasons for its decision to hear Witness Akashi's testimony via video-conference link. On the 24th of August, 2009, the Gotovina Defence orally requested to hear the Witness Akashi's testimony via video-conference link. This request was made in private session and the public is hereby informed of it. The Gotovina Defence argued that video-conference link testimony for Witness Akashi would be in the interests of its client's rights to a expeditious trial, also considering the age of the witness and the distance he would have to travel to come to The Hague. These submissions can be found at transcript pages 20.725. On the 25th of August, 2009, the Prosecution orally responded, not objecting to the Gotovina Defence's request. On the same day, the Chamber granted the request an ordered that Witness Akashi's testimony be heard via video-conference link. The public was informed of this decision on 15th September, 2009. And this can be found at transcript page 21.616. Witness Akashi testified through video-conference link on the 15th and the 16th of September. According to Rule 81 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Chamber may order that proceedings be conducted by way of a video-conference link if it is consistent with the interests of justice. The jurisprudence of this Tribunal has identified three criteria to guide the exercise of the Chamber acting pursuant to this Rule. Those criteria are: The witness is unable or has good reasons to be unwilling to come to the seat of the Tribunal; the witness's testimony is sufficiently important to make it unfair to the requesting party to proceed without it; and the accused are not prejudiced in the exercise of their rights to confront the witness. However, after considering all relevant factors in a particular case, the ultimate determination to be made when considering a request for video-conference link testimony is whether it would be consistent with the interests of justice. Witness Akashi was the UN Secretary-General's special representative to the former Yugoslavia and was acting in the Krajina area during the time-frame covered by the indictment. Accordingly, the Chamber found that the witness's testimony would be sufficiently important to make it unfair to the requesting party to proceed without it. Furthermore, the Chamber found that the accused would not be materially prejudiced in the exercise of their rights to confront the witness if video-conference link were granted. Although the Chamber did not find that Witness Akashi was unable or unwilling for good reasons to come to The Hague, it considered the witness's age, the distance he would have to travel to come to The Hague, and the fact that the Gotovina Defence case was scheduled to be concluded by early September 2009. The Chamber found the amount of time, resources, and effort it would take to arrange for Witness Akashi's appearance in The Hague was not conducive to the expeditious completion of the trial. According, and recalling that there was no objections to the request, the Chamber was satisfied that it would ultimately be consistent with the interests of justice to hear Witness Akashi's testimony via video-conference link. And this concludes the Chamber's reasons on this decision. We will have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, if we could go to a document now, 2D00487. The first page of this document is dated the 12th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But, in fact, we'll go to the second page, please. Page after that, page 3. Or is it page 2? It should be page 2. The next page, please. Page 2 in the Croatian, page 3 in English. Your Honour, this document, at the beginning, has a date on the 12th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see here, dated the -- on the second page, the 30th of August, and it's to the police administrations of Knin through Zadar-Knin, and to Zadar-Knin, and it's from Franjo Djurica. And it's the rules for the joint work of the MUP and UNCIVPOL. And we can see here that the letter refers to UNCRO UNCIVPOL leadership and rules that were developed with the MUP and the Croatian police that were adopted by the leadership and the special envoy, Secretary-General of the UN, Mr. Akashi. And these rules are being sent out on this date, the 30th of August. If we go to the next page, we go to a document headed: "Operational Directives for the Joint Work of the Police." Your Honour, the Court will recognise this as Exhibit P282, and I'm using this document, it's included within it. It's a linked document to this, Your Honour, Exhibit D240 and D53. This concerns joint co-operation between UNCIVPOL and the MUP. We can see here in point 2, Mr. Romanic is -- is mentioned, as well as Mr. Bijelic of the Glina Police Department. And it concerns UNCIVPOL working with the MUP. And in paragraph 4, we can see that problems would be resolved by Mr. Bitanga of Zadar-Knin Police Department. And further on, on the fifth point, that if Mr. Bitanga and Mr. Bobetko can't, Mr. Franjo Djurica would solve problems. And it refers to patrols jointly between UNCIVPOL and the MUP. Mr. Cetina, do you recollect this initiative between your police administration and UNCIVPOL concerning joint procedures to monitor and patrol, in relation to crimes and finding out information?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes. In principle, I do remember. But I don't remember the details, of course, not about the joint patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what connection the Zadar-Knin had with -- with UNCIVPOL? When did communication between UNCIVPOL and your police administration start?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: The first contacts, practical contacts, were between and among my colleagues in Knin. So Knin and the police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And then between your police administration and UNCIVPOL? Can you recollect how long after Operation Storm that you had a joint initiative with them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Roughly 15 to 20 days or a month went by before we had the first meetings with representatives of UNCRO and UNCIVPOL.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And were those meetings helpful? What was your attitude towards them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Our attitude at the beginning was that any information was welcome, from any institution or individual. Any information coming into the police was seen as useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit D1751. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1751 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I now want to turn to another document, which is Exhibit P245. And it's the minutes of a meeting between UNCIVPOL and Mr. Romanic at the Knin police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we can see here that the police structure was discussed with Mr. Romanic, as to the organisation. The CIVPOL structure was discussed, and the agreement we've just been looking at on the joint initiative, Exhibit P282, was discussed. A question of the number of Serbs was raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And then if we go to page 2 of the English and page 2 of the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shootings in the street were raised between UNCIVPOL and Mr. Romanic, and they had a discussion on that and about the police being at the UNCRO camp gate. And then murder cases was raised, and this is what I wanted to direct your attention to. Mr. Romanic was asked about information of certain murder cases observed by the HRAT and CIVPOL during the period after Operation Storm. Mr. Romanic stated that all kind of investigation in the area was going on in Zadar. "The leader of this investigation is Mr. Ive Kardum, whom CIVPOL should address in this matter." And I want you to consider that and comment on it. Was Zadar-Knin Police Administration responsible for all the murder investigations within the Kotar-Knin Police Administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes, there was the crime police department coordinated with the headquarters within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the Kotar-Knin Police Administration have a team of police available to them to investigate any murders within that police administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: That was the only department that was led by Mr. Kardum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So for any murder investigation, Mr. Romanic had to turn and refer the matter to Mr. Kardum; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just turning now to 65 ter 4620.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document from Mr. Elleby, in fact, as the Knin police commander, and it concerns the killing of Sava Babic on the 5th of September and refers to the detail of what the UNMO had seen, and that: "The civilian police is requesting to supervise the investigation of the killing and be present during the investigation of the Croatian police at the scene of the crime." We can see that document. It's probably not a document you've seen before. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And I'm only producing it to have a chain of events, Your Honour. Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit D1752. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can turn now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Can we turn now to Exhibit D230. And this is a letter from Mr. Romanic dated 6th September, 1995, sent to the Zadar-Knin Police Administration, criminal police department. And it concerns the Sava Babic murder that was raised by Mr. Elleby in that memo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he states that following the finding of the killed Sava Babic, UNCIVPOL have requested the civilian police of Knin district police administration, information on the circumstances of her death, and what measures were taken and in what way the on-site investigation was carried out. Was that a correct procedure adopted by Mr. Romanic, in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your police administration receive information from the Kotar-Knin Police Administration of crimes that were being brought to their attention in reports by the UNCIVPOL?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can look here at Exhibit P253.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document sent by the commander of Knin UNCIVPOL, Mr. Romassev, on the 8th of September, 1995. And he lists crimes that were happening. Included within this list of crimes are also killings and bodies, and we can see the nature of the information that was being given by him to the commander of Knin police station. What should the commander of the Knin police station have done with this information received by him from UNCIVPOL?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: As a rule, he should send on the report to the crime department of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And of which police administration would that have been?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: The Zadar-Knin Police Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go to another document now, 2D00246.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's dated the 12th of September, 1995, Knin Police Administration. Sent to the Zadar-Knin Police Administration, duty operations section. Again, information provided by members of UNCRO. We can see, on the 12th of September, 1995, chief of Knin district police administration received information, it says here, from the ZP, Military District of the Croatian Army in Knin, stating that members of UNCRO had found two unknown female bodies, gives the details, and cites the place Brgud in Kistanje municipality. And they stated that the women had die a violent death. We go to the next page of the English, and it refers to a car patrol being sent to the scene. No bodies were found. And at the end, it says: "We will keep you informed about new information in a timely fashion." So Knin reporting in that way to Zadar-Knin on the information provided by UNCRO, was that the correct procedure for dealing with this matter?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, might this document be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit D1753. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, to save court time, similar document to the one we've looked at earlier of the report is Exhibit P262, where Mr. Romassev, again, reports crimes to the Knin police station. I don't go into the detail of that, as I think it will be repetitious, unless the Court would require me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it you want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, to just submit it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just for reference purposes, Exhibit P262. Can we now go to Exhibit D179. And for information purposes, Exhibit P262 includes to reference to that murder in Brgud on the 12th of September, 1995. D179 is under seal so should not be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you look at this document, please, Mr. Cetina. It's from Mr. Elleby, chief of UNCIVPOL in Sector South, and it was sent to you on the 19th of September. And it concerns murders committed since the 4th of August, 1995. And Mr. Elleby attaches a list of all murders reported to UNCIVPOL since the 4th of August, requesting information on the progress of investigations, names of suspects, arrests, charges, any convictions obtained, and requesting to see the files and to discuss the same in a future meeting. We'll just have a look at the pages of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 2 of the English and the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see here listed are various murders on various occasions, or bodies that were found. Do you recollect receiving this report from Mr. Elleby, in relation to these killings within this report?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the end of the report, there's a schedule of 44 names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we can just turn to the next page, again, to see the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were all these murders as listed within this report within your police administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Go through it again. And the next page, just so that can you see the details. And then the page after that. And then turn over again until we get to the schedule at the end. If we can continue through. There we are. If we can just go to the schedule at the end. What did you do about this report when you received it on the 19th of September?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that it's a list of persons who, quite certainly, lost their lives during the war operations, or most of them. And you can see that if you look at the dates when they were found. Part of those persons were certainly murdered as well, that is to say, the crime of murder had been committed against them. Now, this list was sent to the crime police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if these killings had been registered with the crime police already, so that investigations had already started on these killings? Do you know what the situation was?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: I don't remember now, but I'm certain that certain investigations had been started. Others could not have been started because the bodies of these individuals were moved through the sanitisation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what the crime police were able to do to respond to this report?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: It could only have compared the data it had with the inquiries that had -- or investigations that had been started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there a response to Mr. Elleby's request for information and details?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: I am certain that Mr. Elleby was informed of it orally. I'm not sure about written information though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can turn over the page again so that we go to the next page of the list, which is the full number. And then the next page, again, where we have statistics. The next page of the Croatian. There. And if we can turn over again to another part of the report, to the next page, which is headed: "Human rights violations since the 4th of August, 1995." And there listed on several pages are, again, various details. Some of them murders, some looting, some assaults, some discoveries of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What happened to this information headed: "Human rights violations since the 4th of August 1995"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go now to P270.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is another UNCIVPOL document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's not -- no, that's -- the document on the right on my screen isn't the right -- that's right now, yeah. Exhibit P270.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a record of a meeting on the 3rd of October at the Zadar police headquarters, where Mr. Benko, Mr. Nadj, yourself, and a Mr. Hissink, and others were present. And concerned the murder of nine inhabitants in the hamlet of Varivode.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see that the details of that particular matter recorded, including the police being informed on the 28th of September, and that an investigation was started early in the morning of the 29th of September and what happened. And Mr. Marijan Benko and Mr. Ivan Nadj are responsible for the special commission and in charge for the investigation. What was the special commission?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: In fact, following all these various events that had escalated, and once the ministry was informed of all the details, I suppose that the minister and his assistants decided that they should play a more active role in the investigation and that they should join the Zadar-Knin Police Administration in the effort to resolve the murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And were there a series of meetings between members of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration and UNCIVPOL dealing with the investigation into the Varivode killings?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the police was busy working on it independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And did you pass information on to UNCIVPOL to keep them informed as that -- that joint co-operation agreement required?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we certainly informed them of the resolution of the criminal case orally at a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can look at 2D00728. This is a -- it's now D1747. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the minutes of the meeting by UNCIVPOL with Zadar-Knin police authorities, including yourself, in which details of murder cases are revealed and forwarded to the Zadar regional court and criminal proceedings, including the Varivode case. And on page 2 of the English we can see the special investigation team of the interior ministry continues to investigate the most serious cases in Zadar-Knin area of responsibility, and you were given an updated list of incidents recorded by UNCIVPOL. This information that you were giving out to UNCIVPOL concerning the investigations and the criminal proceedings, was that information you could give out to anybody? Was that information generally revealed by your police administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: We could not provide that sort of information to just anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I ask about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are further documents that I have relating to the ongoing relationship between UNCIVPOL and the Zadar-Knin Police Administration concerning the Varivode case, as well as other investigations. Rather than going through that same detail, which is self-explanatory, I propose to bar table that with the Court's approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment, the Chamber does not oppose such a course of action, although there may be some concerns that we might lose sight on details on these matters which can be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, may I exhibit this document. It's dated the 31st of October and on the Varivode series of meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 2D00782. May I have leave to add it to the 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.text: And for reference purposes, the next exhibit that the Court would like to keep an eye on is Exhibit P280, which is a final report by UNCIVPOL on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for this guidance, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, yes. I'm conscious of the time, Your Honour, and I'm just seeing whether I need to introduce any documents in relation to some other matters which can be connected together concerning passing on of information. If we could have 65 ter 2D00771.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document from the International Committee of the Red Cross, and we can see handwritten on it, Mr. Cetina, it's dated Knin, the 7th of September. It's sent to General Cermak. And it concerns crimes that were referred to by the Red Cross from a lady called Carmen Burger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page of the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see a list of crimes, including someone called Milica Dokic, Simon Dukic, Varivode. And this document goes on to refer to other cases. If you could just have a look at them, page by page. Did you receive information from General Cermak that had been referred to him by the International Committee of the Red Cross of crimes that they had been referred to and were concerned about? Did you receive information from Mr. Cermak of reports that were given to him?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: As a rule, such reports did reach us. However, it is possible that I didn't see some of them, due to my presence on the grounds. Still, they would have been received by the chiefs of the departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document becomes Exhibit D1756. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to the name Simo Dukic, there are internal police documents we've discovered which are a complicated series of documents to go through that I would propose to bar table as the story becomes self-evident and the Court has been used to receiving information in this way, either through witnesses or the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if it is introduced in the way bar table documents should be introduced, and you should briefly point to the relevance and briefly describe the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. If we could just turn now to P2649.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document which was sent by you to General Cermak in reply to a request of the International Red Cross organisation for submission of data on incidents that occurred in the area of Knin: "We hereby advise you we have completed the necessary checks regarding each event mentioned in the ICRC letter and established the following ..." And then we see a response.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, this is a document sent by you to General Cermak. And to obtain this information that you sent to General Cermak, where would you have obtained it from?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA
utterances.text: We sent this response, because it was in relation to a request from the ICRC, and that's why we sent it. And we sent it only as information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I can finish now my questioning of the witness, but can I tell the Court there are other documents like this that are self-evident and speak to themselves. And what I propose is that I put them into the chain for the Court and bar table them, because no further purpose would be served in expending further court time on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is what the witness could tell us in addition to what the documents already tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this, then, would conclude your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, this would conclude my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I will have one or two questions for the witness before we adjourn. Mr. Cetina, you remember that a document was shown in which it was described that UNCRO had reported two bodies found in Brgud and that a police car was sent, bodies were not found, and that it would be further investigated the next day. The report dates from the 12th of September, and the report of these bodies was also received on the 12th of September, whereas then on the 13th of September, a further investigation would be -- would take place. Do you have any recollection of that specific incident? Is there any explanation that where UNCRO reports, on the 12th of September, that two human corpses are found, that if the police sends a car over there, that they do not find any bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only one is that they were unable to find the exact location, since the policemen were not locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I assist, Your Honour, because these two documents -- I have two documents relevant to this within this collection here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- which I hope informs the Court. Can we see 2D00775. This is an on-site investigation report compiled on 14th of September, 1995, in Brgud on finding the bodies of two unidentified women. And there is the investigating judge and the account. Your Honour, may I make this document an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- unless Ms. Mahindaratne has --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit D1757. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And to assist the Court further, 2D00772. This is a document dated the 5th of October, 1995, from the crime police Department of Zadar-Knin. And it concerns an on-site investigation. And the document is signed by Mr. Kardum and gives various details of cause of death, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May I make this document an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit D1758. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1758 is admitted into evidence. Then we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Mr. Kay. We'll then adjourn for the day. Mr. Cetina, we'd like to see you back tomorrow, tomorrow in the afternoon, quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom. We adjourn, and we resume on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My colleague reminds me, Mr. Cetina, that I should instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony you have given already or the testimony still to be given in the days to come. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 29th of October, at quarter past 2.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 29th day of October, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
